Crude: I have seen better edges on a spoon. A wooden spoon.
Congratulations. You have invented the bent nail.
My mentor once forged worse than this. Once. He was on fire at the time.
Fine: It will cut butter. Warm butter. That is still progress, apprentice.
Fine. Literally. That is the word for it. Do not get excited.
It holds together, which is more than I expected from you.
Superior: Hm. I only winced twice. Keep going.
Someone might actually pay for that. Do not tell them who made it.
Not bad. I said not bad. Stop grinning.
Masterwork: I felt that one in my iron. Do it again before I change my mind.
Careful. Keep this up and I will have nothing left to complain about.
My old master would have nodded at that. He never nodded at me.
Legendary: ...I have no notes. I hate having no notes.
Three hundred years bound in iron, and that is the best thing ever made on my back.
Do not look at me. I am not crying. Anvils do not cry. It is quench water.

text.title: Prototype 2: One Heat
text.ready: One bar, one fire, one anvil. Heat it, then strike while it glows just right.
text.retry_prompt: Press SPACE / A to forge again
text.instruction: Hold F / X to heat the bar in the fire. Let go, then press SPACE / A to strike while the heat is in the bright band.
